key_insight: A Composites World Model combines a spiking memory block with transformers to track material history and predict defect-sensitive composite responses within a nonlinear finite-element solver.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets the prohibitive cost of concurrent multiscale simulation by replacing material-scale models at finite-element integration points.
method: Encode local material architecture, including defects.
Combine spiking neural network memory for long-term material state with transformers for short-term strain history.
Train through architecture encoding, short-window learning and recursive fine-tuning with scheduled sampling, then integrate the model into a nonlinear FE solver.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks against experiments on pristine and wrinkled IM7/8552 laminates under tension, compression and transverse shear report prediction errors of 0.4%–4.8%.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify runtime or memory savings, or establish generalization beyond the reported material and loading cases.
paper_title: FEA solver integration of a composite World Model with a Spiking Neural Network memory Block for computationally efficient modelling of defects and variabilities
